description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between the NESAC ft model and the SESHA ft model across five different optimization approaches applied to speech data: "Dates," "Americanisms," "Remove Spacing," "Add Spacing," and "Normalised." The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper," with values ranging from 0.000 to 0.003, indicating the magnitude of the improvement or degradation in performance. Each category on the vertical axis has two corresponding horizontal bars: an orange bar for the NESAC ft model and a green bar for the SESHA ft model. The chart shows that for all five optimization approaches, the SESHA ft model consistently achieves a lower WER than the NESAC ft model, as indicated by the green bars being shorter than the orange bars in each group. The specific WER differences are labeled at the end of each bar, with the largest difference observed in the "Normalised" category (0.00323 for NESAC ft and 0.00313 for SESHA ft), and the smallest in the "Dates" category (0.00257 for NESAC ft and 0.00228 for SESHA ft). The bars are arranged in descending order of the difference for the NESAC ft model, with "Normalised" at the top and "Dates" at the bottom.
